evidence: `cargo test` answered "current package believes it's in a workspace when it's not" for every slice; 8 slice runs spent their whole allowance being told correct code was wrong. BENCH_ROUND defaults into bench/rounds, which the root manifest excluded for bench/tasks but not for bench/rounds

defect: A doer burns its whole allowance against an oracle that never ran
evidence: ADR-0057's guard catches a suite that shrank and does not fire when the check cannot execute at all; the doer sees red and has no way to tell a broken oracle from broken code. Found by defect 23, not fixed — the runtime is frozen for this round

defect: A round's first request fails because /health is 200 before any model is loaded
evidence: the first iteration came back 500 "Context size has been exceeded" six seconds in; the router logs show it was still spawning the child instance. n_ctx_slot is 8192 for both models and the message named the wrong cause

defect: No sampling seed is set so no round is reproducible
evidence: the same model on the same slice reached green 6/10 to 10/10; Q7's paired design controls the starting state and not the sampling, so it cannot separate a model's weakness from a bad draw. Budget carries no seed field, so fixing it is a runtime change

defect: A wasted step records the harness's own words and not the model's
evidence: 578 steps across three cells read 'no tool call; nothing happened' and turn.content was discarded, so nothing in the data could say whether the model was planning, refusing, or writing a diff in prose; D6's prompt change had to be designed without it

defect: The model is reloaded on every iteration because the loops alternate
evidence: 122 reloads in one round; the router holds one model under --models-max 1 so each switch reads ~6 GB off disk and pushes it to VRAM, measured at 466% of one core for the two minutes after a spawn. BENCH_BLOCK now groups iterations, default 1 because alternating protects against a 20-point swing between a cell's halves

defect: The model is resident twice: 7.34 GB of private RAM alongside 7.87 GB of VRAM
evidence: Private (7.34 GB) above WorkingSet (6.14 GB) rules out the memory-mapped file, which was the first hypothesis; cause unconfirmed, candidates are the loader keeping a host copy and CUDA pinned staging. Needs one server restart with and without --no-mmap to settle

defect: A round runs with 149 MiB of VRAM to spare and the desktop competes for it
evidence: 7870 of 8192 MiB used on an RTX 3070 with the model loaded; 0.3 GB had already spilled to shared memory, which is system RAM over PCIe. Browsers, Steam, Zoom and VS Code were all holding GPU memory at the same time

defect: The GPU driver version is not recorded anywhere
evidence: cells 1-6 ran on 610.88 and an update to 617.42 was offered mid-round; nothing in round.txt would have said which stack a number came from. Same class as defect 26 — an environment variable that moves the result and that nobody wrote down

defect: The oracle preflight disagreed with the parser it was protecting
evidence: the preflight matched a regular expression shaped like cargo and pytest output; vitest prints 'Tests  26 failed (26)' with no duration, so an all-red scaffolded suite — the correct starting state — read as an oracle that could not run. It now asks the runtime's own counter through bench/src/bin/count.rs

defect: The FINAL row carried a per-language result line that no reader could compare
evidence: 'test result: ok. 26 passed; 0 failed' in Rust, '26 passed' in Python, nothing matchable in TypeScript. Now counted by the same parser and written as ran/passed; analyse.py reads both forms because the earlier rows are committed

defect: Rewriting a file with identical bytes cleared the repeat history
evidence: ADR-0050 §4 resets the detector when an artefact changes, and every successful write counted as a change. A model writing the same bytes forever therefore reset the detector on every step and was never warned; observed as six identical writes with limits.repeats set to 1. Fixed: the bytes are compared first, and the model is told when nothing changed

defect: `ownership` is keyed by file class and was read as keyed by role
evidence: the first draft of the config-to-runtime conversion looked up config.ownership[role] expecting classes; the map is class to roles. Caught by the configuration validator before any run, which named both halves of the mistake

defect: The llama.cpp request was built twice and only one copy was tested
evidence: extracting `body` as a testable seam left `chat` building its own copy, so four wire tests asserted a function production never called. They had already drifted: the temperature reached the shipping copy and not the tested one. Found by a test that failed for the right reason

defect: Every round and probe ran at llama.cpp's default temperature of 0.80
evidence: nobody set it and nobody recorded it, the same class as defect 26. High for code — prose survives a word chosen second-best and code does not compile. The probe watched one model score 5 of 10 then 10 of 10 under identical flags and that was read as the model's variance when it may have been the sampler's
